# /crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Tighten and plan until ready to build](../../from-tighten-and-plan.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Walk a draft spec through architecture, tighten, questions, and the plan until the ready check is clear.

1.141.0: the plan step writes an `## Approval needed` item when a constraint says a named person gives a yes before something. The walk does not write that item itself. An edit confined to that section reopens no step. An unapproved item holds only its tasks (`ready-partial`).

[`/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build`](crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build.md) (1.119.0) is one guided walk with two starts. A playbook path is optional. Without one, step 1 is skipped. Both starts then use the same steps and the same ready check. The walk runs the existing skills. It does not replace them. There is no automatic mode.

Locked order: playbook when given; [`/crav1-review-architecture`](crav1-review-architecture.md) always; [`/crav1-tighten-spec`](crav1-tighten-spec.md) one issue at a time; [`/crav1-resolve-open-questions`](crav1-resolve-open-questions.md); [`/crav1-plan-from-spec`](crav1-plan-from-spec.md), which writes `plan.md` and `tasks.md`; [`/crav1-review-plan`](crav1-review-plan.md) then [`/crav1-tighten-plan`](crav1-tighten-plan.md); [`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md). A step with nothing to do says so and moves on. Research, [`/crav1-review-security`](crav1-review-security.md), [`/crav1-model-data`](crav1-model-data.md), [`/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions`](crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions.md), and [`/crav1-suggest-tests-for-code`](crav1-suggest-tests-for-code.md) are offered only when the spec needs them.

The progress file is `docs/specs/<slug>/walk-progress.md`. It records the step, when, and the version of each file that step covered. Since 1.123.0 the script stamps Done. A later step inside the walk leaves earlier steps done. An optional extra the walk itself runs is recorded with `- Extra:` when it finishes, and that write does not reopen earlier steps. `cover` is optional and only counts a write made outside the walk. A hand edit or [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) between sessions reopens only the steps that change affects. A reopened step blocks the ready check until it is rerun or cleared with nothing new. Spec, plan, and tasks stay the source of truth. The playbook is intake only. After apply, the playbook line is the `docs/playbooks/<topic>.md` path, not the outside path, so resume works on any machine. The walk accepts a `docs/playbooks/` path as its playbook argument. A Blocked or Needs verify row is named back to its step. Needs verify is outside the walk. The walk never reports ready with a blocker, a reopened step, or an open assumption, and it never starts build. Stopping partway is one paused-at line, then Next, Waiting only if blocked, and Uncommitted.

1.125.0: the progress confirm shows the line and gets a yes, unless the step's own confirm already included that record. An extra's yes stays that confirm. An already-applied playbook still asks skip (Recommended) or reapply. Optional extras are offered once, after open questions, when any apply, including show-or-ask when a question is for someone else. Before the plan step is recorded, kept-open questions with no `Blocks:` line are offered, one by one or as one batch.

1.130.0: when the open-questions batch and the progress line share one card, `yes (Recommended)` covers both. Typed changes go on that card's free-text answer. There is no Edits option. The optional-extras card is a multi-select and includes None, go to plan. Skipping does not need a typed word.

1.145.0: the Blocks batch, and the tighten-plan batch inside review-and-tighten-plan, each print a findings table in that same reply before the card. The card names each item and its recommendation, for example `P4 tasks miss the 400 path: A add a test`. It does not say `table above`. The card is not asked without the table.

1.126.0: ready means the first task can start, the rest wait in order, and nothing else blocks. A waits-on-T# reason for a real task is not a blocker. A cycle, or an after: that names no task, still blocks. `readiness --root` builds the rows. When resolve-open-questions is already current, an open question is waiting, not a jump back. Who comes from the latest Asked or Pending line. Next is show-or-ask when the questions are not asked yet, or this walk when the answers arrive. A jump back reruns the owning skill, even for a small patch. The walk does not edit spec.md, plan.md, or tasks.md on that jump, and it does not write Reviewed. A reopened step with nothing new is clear, not a fresh nothing-to-do, and nothing-to-do keeps an earlier done Result. Record one step per call, right when it finishes. record refuses more than one step. Resume warns when two or more steps share a Done stamp.

1.127.0: the playbook question comes before any later step, including a read-only check. Resume may report status and does not start a step. Who comes from the question's "Waiting for" phrase, then the latest Pending or Asked line, or "not named yet", and an unnamed task still counts. Row buckets are waits-in-order, waiting, and blocked. The ready check records Result ready or Result not-ready. An older Result done still reads. `ack-stamps` acknowledges one shared Done stamp after a yes. A new shared stamp warns again.

1.132.0: the ready check also records Result ready-partial when some tasks can start and some are held. A task that depends on a held task is held too. The walk ends, the step is covered, and there is no not-ready mark. Next is [`/crav1-build-tasks`](crav1-build-tasks.md) for the tasks that can start. A later rerun can record ready. not-ready remains when nothing can start, and when a cycle, a missing task, no plan, Needs verify, an assumption, a reopened step, or a jump-back question remains.

1.133.0: the ready-check ending groups ready tasks and held tasks by the build-map row, the same branch as `scripts/build_map.py --recommend`. Order is wave, then map order. A task is `T#` plus its short name. One Next line per ready branch. The walk record stays Result ready-partial.

1.134.0: each locked step, extra, jump back, and the playbook apply path opens that skill's file from this skill's folder (`../crav1-<name>/SKILL.md`, or the reference that step names, including `references/apply.md` and add-to-spec's fact rules). 1.135.0: a spec-tagged finding during plan review is one jump-back card. The recommended option runs [`/crav1-tighten-spec`](crav1-tighten-spec.md) on that finding, by opening `..[`/crav1-tighten-spec`](crav1-tighten-spec.md)/SKILL.md`. The walk then reruns plan-from-spec for the affected parts, review-and-tighten-plan, and the ready check. It does not pause. The other option keeps the finding as an open point and continues. The same finding is offered once. A return is an open point. `walk-progress.md` records `- Jump-back:` and, when it comes back, `- Open point:`, each with `Continue:`. A plan-tagged finding stays in [`/crav1-tighten-plan`](crav1-tighten-plan.md). The ready check compares `tasks.md` with `verify.md`. A ticked task, or a task whose pull request is recorded merged, that `verify.md` still lists as not implemented, or a `Next:` line in `verify.md` that names such a task, makes `verify.md` behind. The check prints `Waiting: [`/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`](crav1-verify-build-against-spec.md) <slug> - verify.md is behind tasks.md (T2, T45)` and does not print that stale Next line. The walk never writes `verify.md` and never runs [`/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`](crav1-verify-build-against-spec.md). It still reaches the ready check, which still rewrites `build-map.md` through [`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md).

1.136.0: a `Next:` line is stale only when it names a ticked task. A merged `[ ]` row whose only leftover is the tick is not behind. A verify-only change does not reopen the ready check and does not force `not-ready`. The result stays `ready` or `ready-partial`, and `verify_waiting` is shown when verify is behind. Where spec, plan, or tasks drift offers a jump back to the ready check, only the walk's record or `clear --yes` restamps `walk-progress.md`. [`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md) only writes `build-map.md`. The spec folder is `..[`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md)/scripts/resolve_spec.py`. Several matches are listed and the run stops. It does not pick the most recently edited tree.

1.137.0: `Spec body:` and `Questions version:` split the spec stamp. An edit confined to `## Open questions` reopens resolve-open-questions and does not reopen tighten-spec, plan-from-spec, review-and-tighten-plan, or tasks-ready-to-build. A question with a `Blocks:` line, or one listed on `Kept questions:`, stays Waiting through that drift. A hold inferred from `T#` ids in the question text stays Waiting too. A reopened resolve-open-questions step alone does not force `not-ready` when some tasks can start: the result is `ready-partial`, with `resolve_waiting` and a Next line for that step. When later steps are reopened, Next is `Next: rerun or clear <steps>.`

1.138.0: a task checkbox, a `(PR n)` or `(done)` note on that task line, and `(PR n)` or a trailing merged word on a Match `Branch:` line are progress. The stamp hashes normalized text and writes `Content stamp: normalized`. Those edits do not reopen a step and do not ask to clear. CRLF and LF match. An older step with no Content stamp line still matches a progress-only edit (raw bytes, the other line ending, one hash-undo, then HEAD once). The next record writes the new line. A sentence change or a renamed branch still reopens. When `result` is `not-ready` and `can_start` is not empty, that list is not a start. Print `because`. It names the reopened steps, or the question that holds the whole slice. A progress-only edit leaves a held slice `ready-partial`.

1.139.0: `scripts/walk_progress.py resolve-stamps` settles a merge conflict in `walk-progress.md` when every hunk is only a version line. [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md) runs it on the pull path. The walk itself does not. A hash is rewritten to the merged file only when the recorded hash matched that side and the merge differs by progress alone. A real edit keeps the upstream hash. `Done` and `Result` stay.

1.143.0: when the result is `ready`, or `ready-partial` with tasks that can start, each Next line recommends [`/crav1-build-walk`](crav1-build-walk.md) with the T number beside the short name and the branch, and names [`/crav1-build-tasks`](crav1-build-tasks.md) as the alternative for one task without the walk. The walk does not run either command. A `not-ready` result does not recommend the walk.

1.144.0: the spec folder command is `<interpreter> -X utf8 <skill crav1-tasks-ready-to-build>/scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs`. On Windows `<interpreter>` is `python` with `PYTHONUTF8=1`. Elsewhere it is `python3`. Do not run `python3` alone. The ready check is `readiness --root <spec-folder>`. Playbook status passes `--playbook <file>` as well as `--root`. The rule is `docs/reference/running-scripts.md`.

1.146.0: `walk_progress.py start --root <folder-or-slug>` resolves a spec folder or a slug the way `resolve_spec.py` does and returns resume and playbook-status in one JSON object. The walk's first step uses that command. A close reword of a recorded spec finding is the same finding: the first-seen `Key:` stays, later wordings are `Alias:`, and the card offers `same recorded finding` or `this is new`. The same P# plus an explicit topic is that id. A different topic is not merged, and two close findings are not merged. An old progress file with only `Key:` still matches those words. A kept question keeps a stable key that ignores a refreshed commit list, and one close reword of a stored question stays that question. The ready check is `readiness --root <spec-folder> --write-map`. It writes `build-map.md` in the same format as [`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md) and the walk does not open that skill. That command stays the standalone list.

A requirement section (Problem, Goals, Non-goals, Users and journeys, Acceptance criteria, Constraints, and the other rows in `references/section-reopen.md`) reopens tighten-spec and the plan steps. It does not reopen resolve-open-questions when `changed_questions` is empty. Ask only those ids. The stable key from 1.146.0 ignores a refreshed commit list, and one close reword of a stored question stays that question. An explicit `Id:` mark still reopens when the words change. `## Match`, `## In the code`, a `Synced at` line, and an already-answered question set `restamp_only` and reopen nothing. An unknown heading reopens the plan. An older step with no `Section stamps` line still uses the 1.137 rule.

1.150.0: `readiness` returns `ending`, and that text is the reply. It prints each held line, one branch per line, with the T# , the short name, and who it waits on. It does not say above, listed above, or earlier output. On ready and ready-partial, `Run next:` is first, before any Waiting line. Each command is alone in a code span and is a complete invocation for a new session: the T#s on that branch, and the slug when `docs/specs` has more than one slice, for example [`/crav1-build-walk`](crav1-build-walk.md) orders-api T3`. One slice needs no slug. The next line names the branch and the short task name. The full Next lines stay after that. A reopened tasks-ready-to-build step is not a blocker. The result comes from the rows, and the reply says once that the earlier record is replaced. Another reopened step still forces not-ready. Clear with nothing new is unchanged.

1.151.0: the walk fetches the specs repo before it reads. Behind or diverged, it stops and Run next is `git pull --no-rebase`. A task with an `In progress:` line in `claims.md` is left unchanged, and the walk says once which claimed tasks were kept. The ready check holds those tasks as `in progress by <user> since <date>` and does not offer them in Run next. A claim older than three days, or `Claim max age:`, warns and is never cleared on its own.

1.152.0: the ready check's Next lines match Run next, and `M can start now` counts only ready branches. `scripts/repo_sync.py` and `scripts/claims.py` in this skill are thin wrappers to the build-walk copies. A mid-walk stop does not clear a claim.

1.154.0: the walk's references match the 1.153.0 ending: one Run next block at the top, the walk command only there, and no `Next:` line after the Waiting lines. A stop prints the walk command in a Run next entry, not a `Next:` line. The ending adds one `Loop:` line per pair or ring of branches that wait for each other, and those tasks count as Blocked in the counts and in `build-map.md`. Other tasks keep their state, so the result can stay `ready-partial`. Kit lint fails when a skill file tells the agent to write a Next line after the Waiting lines.

## Runs when

A spec should be tightened and planned until it is ready to build. Called by the user.

## Prompts

The walk's own prompts are the playbook skip or reapply question, asked even when that file is already applied, one batch of optional extras once after open questions when any extra applies, one batch for kept-open questions that still have no Blocks line after the plan, one jump-back card per spec finding during plan review (recommended: run /crav1-tighten-spec on just that finding now; the other option keeps it as an open point and continues; a finding already jumped does not ask again), one same-or-new card when a spec finding is a close reword of a recorded finding (same recorded finding, or this is new), one jump-back question when the ready check is not clear (jump back, or clear a reopened step with nothing new), and the yes before the progress file is written. A reopened tasks-ready-to-build step does not ask that jump-back card (1.150.0). That yes shows the progress line, unless the step's own confirm already included this record. An extra's yes is that case. Questions inside a step belong to that step's skill and its own budget. A value the user left out is outside the budget. A headless run stops before any of these. A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: The spec folder, an optional playbook (outside the project or under `docs/playbooks/`), and the progress file when one exists.

Reads the spec folder, the optional playbook, and `walk-progress.md` when resuming. The first command is `scripts/walk_progress.py start --root <folder-or-slug>`, which returns resume and playbook-status. The ready check is `scripts/walk_progress.py readiness --root <spec-folder> --write-map`, which reads `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `claims.md` when it exists, and `verify.md` through `task_order.py` and `question_blocks.py`. It fetches the specs repo before it reads. It does not read production data.

## Writes

In short: `docs/specs/<slug>/walk-progress.md` after a yes, `build-map.md` from the ready check, and the `docs/playbooks/` path when a playbook was applied. The playbook copy is written by apply.

Writes `docs/specs/<slug>/walk-progress.md` through `scripts/walk_progress.py`, and only after a yes that was shown the progress line, unless that step's confirm already included the record. One record per step, right when that step finishes. A spec-finding jump back records `- Jump-back:` with `Continue:`, and a return records `- Open point:`. A close reword records `Alias:` on the first-seen `Key:`. `readiness --write-map` writes `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md` in the same format as [`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md). The playbook step records `docs/playbooks/<topic>.md`, not the outside path. Spec, plan, and task edits happen inside the skill the walk runs, after that skill's own yes, except a `Blocks:` line (and the matching Risk sentence when it is `Blocks: none` or `Blocks: whole slice`) for a kept-open question that still has no line after the plan. The whole slice writes `- Blocks: whole slice` and the Risk line `kept open; blocks the whole slice until resolved.` A `Blocks:` line wins over that Risk wording. A jump back reruns that skill and does not edit those files, and it does not write `Reviewed:`. [`/crav1-resolve-open-questions`](crav1-resolve-open-questions.md) with `apply <file>` writes playbook answers and the `docs/playbooks/` copy, including Kept items through the rules of [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md), and this walk does not call [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) a second time for those items.

## Does not

Leaves `spec.md`, `plan.md`, and `tasks.md` to the skills that own them, except that one `Blocks:` pass. Does not change `Answer:` or `Change:` lines in the playbook. Does not start [`/crav1-build-tasks`](crav1-build-tasks.md), [`/crav1-build-features`](crav1-build-features.md), or [`/crav1-verify-build-against-spec`](crav1-verify-build-against-spec.md). Never writes `verify.md`. Does not git-commit.

Limits and exceptions: A headless run stops. No playbook skips step 1. Architecture review always runs inside the walk even though the new-slice route marks it optional. Needs verify is named and not started. An open plan-review warning is not ready. The progress script does not decide that a playbook was already applied unless this walk recorded that apply.

## You run next / Runs by itself

- You run next: [`/crav1-build-walk`](crav1-build-walk.md); [`/crav1-build-tasks`](crav1-build-tasks.md)
- Runs by itself: Opens each locked skill's file from this skill's folder and follows it, including [`/crav1-resolve-open-questions`](crav1-resolve-open-questions.md) `references/apply.md` on yes when a playbook is applied. The ready check does not open [`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`](crav1-tasks-ready-to-build.md). It runs `readiness --write-map`. It does not start those skills as slash commands. It does not run Build.
